# braintrust_dataset (Resource)

Manages a Braintrust [dataset](https://docs.braintrust.dev/annotate/datasets). Datasets belong to a project and store evaluation data.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "braintrust_project" "my_project" {
  name = "my-project"
}

# Create a dataset within a project
resource "braintrust_dataset" "evaluation_data" {
  project_id  = braintrust_project.my_project.id
  name        = "evaluation-data"
  description = "Golden dataset for model evaluation"
  tags        = ["gold", "reviewed"]
  metadata_json = jsonencode({
    owner = "evaluation-team"
    tier  = 1
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the dataset. Within a project, dataset names are unique.
- `project_id` (String) Unique identifier for the project that the dataset belongs to.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Textual description of the dataset.
- `metadata_json` (String) JSON-encoded dataset metadata object. Use the JSON literal null to clear it.
- `tags` (List of String) Dataset tags. Use an empty list to clear all tags.

### Read-Only

- `created` (String) Date of dataset creation.
- `deleted_at` (String) Date of dataset deletion, or null if the dataset is still active.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier for the dataset (UUID).
- `url_slug` (String) URL slug assigned to the dataset by Braintrust.
- `user_id` (String) Identifies the user who created the dataset.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by the dataset ID.
terraform import braintrust_dataset.example 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```
